message.content:
Below is a quick‑reference guide for pulling *detailed* interface data from a few common platforms (Cisco IOS/IOS‑XE, Juniper Junos, Linux, Windows). Feel free to let me know if you’re working with a different vendor or want a specific script/API example. --- ## 1. CLI – “Show” / “Display” Commands | Platform | Command | Typical Output Fields | |----------|---------|-----------------------| | **Cisco IOS / IOS‑XE** | `show interface `
`show interface detail` | • Interface name
• Status (up/down)
• Protocol status
• MAC address
• Speed & duplex
• MTU
• Input/output counters (bytes, packets, errors, discards)
• Last input/output timestamps | | **Juniper Junos** | `show interfaces `
`show interfaces extensive` | • Interface name
• Link status
• Physical & logical addresses
• Media type, speed, duplex
• MTU
• Traffic counters (in/out bytes, packets, errors, discards)
• Last change time | | **Linux** | `ip -d link show `
`ifconfig ` | • Interface name
• Flags (UP, BROADCAST, RUNNING, MULTICAST)
• MAC address
• MTU
• RX/TX bytes, packets, errors, dropped, overruns, frame
• RX/TX queue lengths | | **Windows** | `Get-NetAdapter -Name ""`
`Get-NetIPConfiguration -InterfaceAlias ""` | • Adapter name
• Status (Up/Down)
• MAC address
• Link speed
• IPv4/IPv6 configuration (addresses, subnet mask, gateway)
• Statistics (BytesIn, BytesOut, PacketsIn, PacketsOut, Errors) | ### Example – Cisco IOS ```text Router# show interface GigabitEthernet0/1 GigabitEthernet0/1 is up, line protocol is up Hardware is Gigabit Ethernet, address is 001b.2c3d.4e5f (bia 001b.2c3d.4e5f) MTU 1500 bytes, BW 1000000 Kbit/sec, DLY 10 usec, reliability 255/255, txload 1/255, rxload 1/255 Encapsulation ARPA, loopback not set Keepalive set (10 sec) Full-duplex, 1000Mb/s, media type is RJ45 ... 5 minute input rate 2000 bits/sec, 3 packets/sec 5 minute output rate 3000 bits/sec, 4 packets/sec 0 packets input, 0 bytes, 0 no buffer Received 0 broadcasts, 0 runts, 0 giants, 0 throttles 0 input errors, 0 CRC, 0 frame, 0 overrun, 0 ignored 0 packets output, 0 bytes, 0 underrun, 0 output errors ``` --- ## 2. SNMP – OID Lookup | Metric | Common OID (RFC1213) | Notes | |--------|---------------------|-------| | Interface description | `.1.3.6.1.2.1.2.2.1.2.` | Human‑readable name | | Admin status | `.1.3.6.1.2.1.2.2.1.7.` | 1=up, 2=down, 3=testing | | Oper status | `.1.3.6.1.2.1.2.2.1.8.` | 1=up, 2=down, 3=testing | | MAC address | `.1.3.6.1.2.1.2.2.1.6.` | 6 octets | | In octets | `.1.3.6.1.2.1.2.2.1.10.` | 64‑bit counter | | Out octets | `.1.3.6.1.2.1.2.2.1.16.` | 64‑bit counter | | In errors | `.1.3.6.1.2.1.2.2.1.14.` | Count of inbound errors | | Out errors | `.1.3.6.1.2.1.2.2.1.20.` | Count of outbound errors | **Python example (using pysnmp):** ```python from pysnmp.hlapi import * def snmp_get(host, community, oid): iterator = getCmd(SnmpEngine(), CommunityData(community), UdpTransportTarget((host, 161)), ContextData(), ObjectType(ObjectIdentity(oid))) errorIndication, errorStatus, errorIndex, varBinds = next(iterator) if errorIndication: print(errorIndication) elif errorStatus: print('%s at %s' % (errorStatus.prettyPrint(), errorIndex and varBinds[int(errorIndex)-1][0] or '?')) else: for varBind in varBinds: return varBind[1].prettyPrint() print(snmp_get('192.168.1.1', 'public', '.1.3.6.1.2.1.2.2.1.2.1')) # ifDescr for ifIndex 1 ``` --- ## 3. NETCONF – XML RPC | Operation | Request | Response | |-----------|---------|----------| | Get interface info | `ge-0/0/1` | `ge-0/0/1…` | | Get all interfaces | `` | List of all interfaces with stats | **Python (ncclient) example:** ```python from ncclient import manager with manager.connect(host='10.0.0.1', port=830, username='admin', password='admin', hostkey_verify=False) as m: filter_xml = ''' ge-0/0/1 ''' reply = m.get(filter=filter_xml) print(reply.xml) ``` --- ## 4. RESTCONF – JSON API | Endpoint | Method | Description | |----------|--------|-------------| | `/restconf/data/interfaces/interface=` | GET | Returns JSON with interface state, config, and statistics | | `/restconf/data/interfaces/interface=/statistics` | GET | Only the counters section | **Curl example:** ```bash curl -k -u admin:admin https \ -H "Accept: application/yang-data+json" \ https://10.0.0.1/restconf/data/interfaces/interface=GigabitEthernet0%2F1 ``` Sample JSON snippet: ```json { "ietf-interfaces:interface": [ { "name": "GigabitEthernet0/1", "oper-status": "up", "enabled": true, "ietf-ip:ipv4": { ... }, "ietf-if-type:phys-address": "00:1b:2c:3d:4e:5f", "ietf-netconf-with-defaults:statistics": { "in-octets": 123456789, "out-octets": 987654321, "in-errors": 0, "out-errors": 0 } } ] } ``` --- ## 5. Windows PowerShell – CIM/WMI ```powershell Get-CimInstance -ClassName Win32_NetworkAdapter -Filter "NetConnectionID='Ethernet'" | Select-Object Name, NetEnabled, MACAddress, Speed, AdapterType, Description Get-CimInstance -ClassName Win32_PerfFormattedData_Tcpip_NetworkInterface | Where-Object {$_.Name -eq 'Ethernet'} | Select-Object Name, BytesTotalPerSec, PacketsReceivedPerSec, PacketsSentPerSec ``` --- ## Quick Checklist for “Detailed” Data 1. **Identification** – name, alias, description, physical address (MAC), logical address (IP). 2. **State** – admin status, oper status, last change timestamp. 3. **Link properties** – speed, duplex, MTU, media type, auto‑negotiation status. 4. **Traffic counters** – in/out bytes, packets, errors, discards, collisions, overruns. 5. **Error specifics** – CRC, frame, alignment, runts, giants, input/output drops. 6. **Performance metrics** – latency, jitter, packet loss (usually via SNMP traps or external monitoring). --- ### Need a Script? If you’d like a ready‑to‑run script for a particular platform (e.g., a Bash one‑liner for Linux, a PowerShell module for Windows, or a Python library for NETCONF/RESTCONF), just tell me the target OS/vendor and I’ll generate it for you.
